paper_title: Optimal Mixing for two-State Anti-Ferromagnetic Spin Systems
authors: Xiaoyu Chen (Nanjing University, China), Weiming Feng (University of Edinburgh, China; University of Edinburgh, United Kingdom), Yitong Yin (Nanjing University, China), Xinyuan Zhang (Nanjing University, China)
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 7
statement: Compared to the classes of two-spin systems resolved in [7, 8], the uniqueness criterion (Condition I.2) used in Theorem I.3 still leaves open the optimal mixing for the following classes of anti-ferromagnetic two-spin systems (β, γ, λ) on G: • γ > 1, the graph G is a general graph with maximum degree Δ, and (β, γ, λ) is d-unique for all 1 ≤ d < Δ (i.e. up-to-Δ-unique), that is, the “skewed” anti-ferromagnetic case (where γ > 1) on general irregular graphs. The main technical difficulty for this case is that the MLS constant for such case was very much under-studied, even in much sub-critical regimes, so there lacks a MLSI for the “easier” regime from where we can apply our boosting theorem (Theorem I.12) for MLSI. Another minor technical difficulty is that the marginal stability asserted by Condition I.11 does not hold for this case in general. However, we believe that this can be circumvented because what Condition I.11 asserts is just a sufficient condition for the product domination property. And we conjecture that for any anti-ferromagnetic two-spin system satisfying the upto-Δ-uniqueness, the k-transformed distribution μk satisfies the proper product domination property for all sufficiently large k. Verifying this conjecture would imply the optimal mixing for the above “skewed” anti-ferromagnetic two-spin systems on general irregular graphs, if a MLSI is also proved in an easier regime when assuming the up-to-Δ-uniqueness.
